 ACA Marketplace Numbers Plunging as Open Enrollment Period Nears
 By 
 Julie Carter 
 October 22, 2026 
 No Comments 
 Loading the Elevenlabs Text to Speech AudioNative Player… 
 Affordable Care Act (ACA) open enrollment is set to begin on November 1 . This year, prospective enrollees may face new headwinds as they attempt to find coverage. Congress declined to extend enhanced ACA subsidies late last year, undermining access and affordability. Experts predicted millions would lose coverage as a result. A new report from KFF finds that indeed, over 4.6 million fewer people are enrolled in ACA plans as of June 2026 compared to June last year.
 Congress declined to extend enhanced ACA subsidies last year, undermining access and affordability.
 How We Got Here
 During the pandemic, Congress put in place enhanced premium tax credits that helped low- and middle-income people afford health coverage through the ACA Marketplace. These credits expired at the end of 2025, leading to effective price hikes on top of huge spikes in ACA premiums .
 The premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025, leading to effective price hikes on top of huge spikes in ACA premiums.
 At the time, KFF estimated that, without the subsidies in place, beginning in 2026 more than 22 million people could see their premiums rise by 75% on average , while people in rural areas could see a 90% increase . KFF projected that people 50 to 64 years old would be especially hard hit by the changes . AARP predicted the same .
 Due to the expiration and other rule changes, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimated that Marketplace enrollment would drop by 25% by the end of 2026.
 What Is Happening Now
 KFF’s new research shows that Marketplace enrollment declined 18% year-over-year as of June 2026. The report notes more coverage losses are likely in the second half of 2026 as more people fall behind in their payments and as repercussions from plan cancellations become clear . . Inflation is also taking more out of people’s paychecks each month, which can lead to agonizing choices about how to spend limited dollars.
 The Future
 ACA enrollment losses will likely continue in 2027. Premiums are again increasing sharply , meaning even more people could be priced out of coverage.
 Many will have nowhere to turn. Major HR 1 eligibility changes are taking effect or looming.
 And many will have nowhere to turn. Major HR 1 eligibility changes are taking effect or looming in the new year. This includes loss of Medicare coverage and other limits to health insurance for many lawful immigrants who have paid into the system, and administrative barriers for expansion Medicaid .
 These rules and restrictions are expected to drive up the number of uninsured, especially among lower income and legal immigrant populations . Overall, CBO estimates that 11.8 million people will become uninsured due to HR 1 . When combined with external policy changes, such as the expiration of enhanced ACA subsidies, this number climbs to nearly 17 million .
 Rising Uninsured Numbers Harm Everyone
 As more people become uninsured, everyone pays. Individuals go without needed care, which harms their health, well-being, and economic security. The health system cannot absorb what is expected to be billions of dollars in uncompensated care and many hospitals and other providers could be forced to close . And programs like Medicare pay more when uninsured people reach eligibility sicker than they would have been if they had access to care.
 The health system cannot absorb what is expected to be billions of dollars in uncompensated care.
 Medicare Rights urges policymakers to reverse course on policies that make it harder to afford, get, and keep coverage. As affordability declines and HR 1’s barriers go into place, more people will be at risk of going without needed care, and of experiencing the fallout—including worse health, financial instability, and diminished well-being. Older adults, people with disabilities, and others with complex care needs are likely to be especially harmed, along with the programs on which they rely.
